For Connected Device Programs

Device Passport™: Digital Product Passport Software for Connected Devices

Device Passport is digital product passport software that gives every device in an Apkudo-powered program a verified record of what it is, what it is worth, and where it has been. That record lets teams decide, on trusted data, what each device is worth and where it should go next. Carriers, device manufacturers (OEMs), insurers, enterprises, and logistics providers use that record from trade-in and testing to resale, recovery, and recycling.

One Record per Device

What Is a Device Passport?

A Device Passport is a persistent, verifiable record of one device's identity, condition, history, and value across its entire lifecycle. The Device Passport Platform creates and maintains it, applying the idea behind the EU digital product passport (DPP) to each individual device.

Image: a small Device Passport visual

Problem > Solution

What a Device Passport Fixes in Device Programs

In most device programs, the record does not travel with the device, so each new partner verifies the device again from scratch.

Challenge

With a Device Passport

Grading by hand is subjective: manual testing assigns an inaccurate cosmetic grade roughly half of the time, which leads to disputes and wrong valuations across channels.

Condition data is captured by Apkudo automation in a controlled testing environment, so grading results stay consistent instead of drifting with light and sound.

Consumers distrust grading outcomes they cannot see, and trade-ins that require a store visit or a clunky third-party app see lower attach rates.

Consumers run the Diagnostic SDK check in your own app from home, and the final payout can follow once a processing facility validates the device.

Warranty and protection claims arrive for devices the customer no longer owns, already repaired elsewhere, or enrolled twice, and nothing in the claim shows it.

A real-time device history is checked before a claim is approved, so each decision rests on the device's verified record.

Manual intake and processing depend on people, so a seasonal peak, such as a new phone launch, means hiring and retraining staff.

Automation processes devices without additional human interaction and scales up and down as device volumes shift, so peaks need no new hiring and retraining.

Devices that sit idle lose residual value every day, and a device sent to the wrong next step leaves recovery value on the table.

Device AI™ routes each device to its next step from early, objective condition data, instead of a manual call on incomplete information.

Program owners see only what happens inside each partner's own network, so visibility arrives late, and manual records leave no audit trail when a dispute arises.

Partners work from the same record, updated in real time, and each entry shows who recorded it, where, when, and in which program.

Inside the Record

What a Device Passport Looks Like

  1. 1

    Passport Directory

    Every device with date added, model, make, carrier lock, and status, such as Triage, Repair, or Storage.

  2. 2

    Device Header

    The IMEI, when the device was received, and where it sits now.

  3. 3

    Overview Tiles

    Diagnostics score, carrier lock, erasure, battery health, cosmetic grade, and value at a glance.

  4. 4

    Record Tabs

    Overview, History, Media, and Diagnostics tabs open the full record.

  5. 5

    Diagnostics Summary

    A pass or fail result for each functional check, with the cosmetic grade beside it.

From First Test to Last Handoff

How the Device Passport Works

Each record is identified by device identifiers such as the IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) shown in the header of its passport. In a consumer app, the Diagnostic SDK shows a unique QR code on screen to confirm the right device is assessed. Device Shell™ connected packaging, which keeps a device sealed from grading to delivery, carries a permanent etched identifier linked to the record.

  1. 01
    01

    Capture at Every Handoff

    When a device is received, inspected, or graded, data collection runs through Apkudo automation or the Diagnostic SDK, and partner and third-party data sources add to the device's record.

  2. 02
    02

    Write the Record

    Each event joins the device's history of identity, condition, repairs, and value; earlier events stay, and each data point traces to an actor, time, facility, and program.

  3. 03
    03

    Decide the Next Step

    Device AI™ scores and grades each device from its record, based on real-time data, and routes it to its next step: resale, repair, or recycling.

  4. 04
    04

    Share With the Next Partner

    The verified data is shared with internal teams and external partners, each seeing the view its role needs, so the next partner starts from the existing record.

Platform Foundation

The Architecture of the Device Economy

Realizing the full value of the Device Passport requires a new way of working. The Apkudo Platform is organized into four essential layers designed to turn fragmented supply chain and device data into a single, actionable source of truth.

The Operating System

Apkudo Platform

The foundational operating system for the device economy. Our platform replaces disconnected data and manual work with one source of truth. It is the infrastructure that connects your systems and devices to provide the ground-truth data you need to move faster.

The Record

Device Passport

By pulling ground-truth data from every system, software, and hardware touchpoint, the Device Passport creates a validated history that enables faster decisions and higher resale margins.

The Intelligence

Device AI™

Smarter decisions, automated. This is the intelligence layer that scores, grades, and routes your devices based on real-time data. It replaces subjective human judgment with objective data, so you can scale your operations without losing accuracy.

The Execution Layer

Device OS™

The bridge between software and action. Device OS is the universal language that allows our platform to communicate directly with hardware. It powers our precision automation and integrates with partner equipment, from robots and scanners to diagnostic tools.

Regulation and Standards

Getting Passport-Ready for the EU Digital Product Passport

Device Passport already keeps an item-level record of each device's identity, condition, and history.

In the EU, digital product passport requirements are set product group by product group through delegated acts under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (EU) 2024/1781. Each act sets which DPP data a product must carry. The record alone does not mean your products meet those requirements.

GSMA Device Homologation Pilot

For its 2026 Device Homologation Pilot, GSMA partnered with Apkudo to provide the data-sharing environment on Apkudo's Device Passport Platform. Through policy-based access control, manufacturers keep ownership of their data, and regulators get permissioned data access for a stated purpose.

Key EU Dates

12 July 2023

Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 adopted

13 June 2024

Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation adopted

18 February 2027

a battery passport is required for each light means of transport (LMT) battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh, and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service

How Device Passport Pricing Works

A program has no price tag of its own. It is a bundle of priced capabilities, such as robotic automation or the Diagnostic SDK, configured to solve your problem, and each capability carries its own commercial terms. A platform fee applies to every customer, whatever capabilities they use. Device testing, the as-a-service offers, and implementation and professional services are paid for where a program needs them.

Frequently Asked Questions

A digital product passport is a digital record of product data, accessible through data carriers such as barcodes and QR codes. Under the EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, its contents are set per product group. Device Passport keeps a record of this kind for each connected device; on its own, it does not meet the passport requirements that a delegated act sets for a product group.

The Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation describes the passport as a tool for making product information available along the value chain and improving traceability. A Device Passport applies the same idea to one device: a verified history shared with the internal teams and external partners that handle it.

In the EU, it becomes mandatory product group by product group. Under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, a product whose delegated act sets digital product passport requirements can only be placed on the EU market or put into service if one is available. The EU Battery Regulation requires a battery passport for light means of transport (LMT), industrial (over 2 kWh), and electric vehicle batteries from 18 February 2027. Portable batteries are not on that list.

With Apkudo, a Device Passport program starts in five steps, from a first conversation through contracting to program setup. A trade-in program can be integrated and configured in as little as five weeks, depending on its type and scale.

For connected devices, Apkudo provides a Device Passport: a digital product passport solution that builds the record each time a device is handled, from first-party diagnostics captured by its own automation and the Diagnostic SDK, plus partner and third-party data.

Apkudo is used to run device programs on trusted data. Carriers, OEMs, insurers, enterprises, and logistics providers use it for programs such as trade-in, warranty, repair, enterprise device recovery, and resale. Each program generates verified device data that builds each device's passport.
